name: azure-openai-stream
purpose: AZURE_OPENAI source, STREAMING: the provider body is piped through the shared forwardFetchResponse, so the frames the mock writes reach the caller unchanged and the backend sets no content type. Its control is azure-openai-nonstream, which carries the SAME answer text through the buffered path.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: the recording peer's origin is supplied in the request body (azure_base_url = <mock>), so only the PATH and QUERY are the compared contract
tier2.reason: AZURE_OPENAI has NO pinned base URL: chat-completions.js:1689 reads azure_base_url from the request body, so both legs are aimed at the peer by the DRIVER.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
